diagram_classification: theological (Trinitarian diagram, a form of the Scutum Fidei or Shield of the Trinity)
interpretation: The diagram sets out the doctrine of the Trinity. Three outer roundels, PATER (Father), SPIRITUS SANCTUS (Holy Spirit, abbreviated and hard to read) and FILIUS (Son), sit at the corners of an inverted triangle. Each is joined to the central roundel DEUS (God) by a band labelled EST ("is"). The three outer sides of the triangle, which link the Persons to one another, are labelled NON EST ("is not"). The diagram therefore says that the Father is God, the Son is God and the Holy Spirit is God, while the Father is not the Son, the Son is not the Holy Spirit and the Holy Spirit is not the Father. The Persons are distinct from one another yet each is the one divine essence. The crucified Christ drawn on the line between DEUS and FILIUS stresses the Son's incarnation and Passion. It places the second Person, who is God, at the centre of the Trinitarian formula.
evidence: The roundels carry the transcribed words PATER, FILIUS, a Spirit label (Spiritus Sanctus, abbreviated) and DEUS in the centre. The three radial bands read EST and the three sides of the triangle read NON EST. This matches the well-known Trinitarian formula diagram. The crucifix is a visible figure on the DEUS–FILIUS axis. The faint circular pattern behind the diagram looks like show-through from another page and is not part of the diagram.
